Governed production planning for approved Content Packages — eligibility checks, deterministic mode/provider recommendation, asset readiness scoring, budget governance, human approval, and Manual Export briefs. Never executes a provider or generates a video; that is future-milestone scope.

Governed runtime that executes ready, approved Production Jobs: execution eligibility, a file-backed FIFO queue, execution locking, bounded retries, provider polling, cancellation, and artifact ingestion. Supported today: the Manual Export adapter (production-safe, no credentials) and an optional Mock Video test adapter (disabled unless PROVIDER_MOCK_VIDEO_ENABLED=true, never a real video). Not supported: real third-party video execution (HeyGen/Higgsfield/HyperFrames/OpenArt Video have no execution adapter yet), background workers, or auto-publishing.

Real HeyGen video generation through the Provider Execution Engine via HeyGen's official Remote MCP server (OAuth 2.1 + PKCE, billed against the user's HeyGen web-plan premium credits — no API key). Supported when validated: OAuth connection, account discovery, avatar discovery, voice discovery, avatar_video and talking_head modes, async submit, polling, local artifact ingestion. Conditionally supported: captions, voice speed, test-submission bookkeeping (cancellation is NOT conditionally supported — see below). Not supported: cancellation of an in-flight render (no such HeyGen MCP tool exists), the Direct API, template-based generation, interactive/streaming avatars, auto-publishing, batch generation, and an exact pre-generation cost (no credit/estimate tool exists on this account). Not yet marked fully production-active — that requires one explicitly approved live generation to succeed first.

Local-machine HyperFrames production workflow — composition discovery, lint, check, render, preview, and secure artifact import, driven entirely from inside Mika OS via a fixed local command runner (no arbitrary shell commands). Supported: discovering compositions under tools/hyperframes/, lint --json, check --json, render (quality standard|high, low-memory-first worker defaults), a preview server started/stopped by direct process ownership (not the CLI's own path-based --status/--stop tracking), a one-click Render-and-Import flow that stops on lint or check failure and never auto-approves the result, idempotent import into a local Production Job (provider hyperframes-local, metadata.isLocalRender: true) reusing the same artifact-store/job-store/Universal-Output-Viewer pipeline as every other production output. Not supported: a remote HyperFrames API or MCP adapter, execution through the Provider Execution Engine, background workers, concurrent renders per composition, or CLI-driven dimension/orientation rewriting (HyperFrames output dimensions are fixed by the composition itself).

Governed preparation and manual publishing of approved production outputs across TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, LinkedIn, Pinterest, X, and Facebook Reels. Publish Jobs only ever reference an existing production artifact — never duplicate media, never generate content, never edit media, never rerun a provider. The review gate (review.status === 'approved') is never bypassed. Supported: manual publishing (explicit user attestation), publish scheduling (metadata only), platform validation (honest warnings, never silent media edits), and complete manual export bundles (ZIP, JSON, Markdown). Does not support: automatic/API publishing, a background scheduler or automatic execution, OAuth, or any platform API uploads — every platform adapter in v1 is manual-export only.
